correctness.rationale: In hopping units the generator is A=-iH/J-(k/2)P_0, k=Gamma/J. Its eigenvalue real part equals -k|v_0|^2/(2||v||^2). A zero real part forces v_0=0 and v_2=-v_1; this is possible only at sin(phi)=0, when the dark eigenvector has squared overlap 1/2 with the initial state and stationary survival mass 1/2. Otherwise A is strictly stable. I solved the adjoint integral equation A^*K+KA=-I independently in the bright/dark basis with a real rational half-angle parameter, covering every nondark flux. The initial expectation of K is 3/k+1/(2s)+k/(4s^2) with s=sin(phi); dividing by J restores physical time and confirms the sign for the frozen Hamiltonian. Completing the square in 1/s gives the nearest feasible point to -1/k on (-infinity,-1] union [1,infinity). It yields exactly two optimizing phases when k<1, and only 3pi/2 at and above k=1, with the two stated minimum values.
